items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Psychology or related field (Preferred)
Minimum 1 year of experience implementing or supporting PEERs program
Experience in a healthcare, behavioral health, or academic medical setting (preferred)
Minimum 1 year of experience working with neurodivergent and/or autistic individuals (preferred)
Experience with EPIC/CareConnect or other electronic medical record systems (preferred)

The UCLA Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking a full-time Program Assistant to support the UCLA PEERS Clinic. The PEERS Clinic serves children, adolescents, and adults with developmental neurodevelopment disabilities, supporting innovative programs that promote inclusion, independence, and quality of life.

In this role you will provide administrative, patient service, and program support to faculty, staff, clinicians, and program participants while helping ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the clinic. Key responsibilities:
Schedule appointments and coordinate faculty and clinician calendars
Check in patients, enter information into CareConnect, and assist with MyChart activation
Support participant screenings, enrollment, and program coordination activities
Monitor patient communications and assist with clinic operations
Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, meeting agendas, and minutes
Coordinate meetings, maintain files and records, and support special projects
Assist with travel reimbursements, purchasing requests, credentialing paperwork, and other administrative functions
Provide administrative support during group and individual program sessions
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, and Excel

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Knowledge of psychiatric or mental health terminology (preferred)
Ability and comfort working with the departments patient population and their families
Strong organizational, communication, or customer service skills
Ability to maintain confidentiality and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgement with minimal supervision
